en.name: Albert the Great
en.summary: Thirteenth-century Dominican friar, scientist, and Doctor of the Church who was the teacher of Thomas Aquinas.
en.body: Albert was a German Dominican friar whose encyclopedic curiosity spanned theology, philosophy, botany, zoology, astronomy, and chemistry, earning him the title Doctor Universalis for the breadth of his learning and a reputation as one of the most important natural scientists of the Middle Ages. He was instrumental in introducing the newly recovered works of Aristotle to Western Christian scholarship, arguing that reasoned philosophical inquiry and Christian faith were compatible rather than opposed, an approach his most famous student, Thomas Aquinas, would carry to its fullest expression. He also served briefly as bishop of Regensburg before returning to teaching and writing, and personally defended Aquinas's orthodoxy after his death when some of his teachings came under attack. He died in 1280 and was canonized and declared a Doctor of the Church simultaneously by Pope Pius XI in 1931, who also named him patron of natural scientists.
